translationRepairs: Some say: yiyin carried a tripod and urged Tang to become king; Baili Xi fed oxen under a cart and Duke Mu employed him to become hegemon. They made themselves fit first, then led them to the great way.

Some say: Yi Yin carried a tripod and urged Tang to become king; Baili Xi fed oxen under a cart and Duke Mu employed him to become hegemon. They made themselves fit first, then led them to the great way.
Chinese 伊尹 is the personal name Yi Yin; idiomatic “yiyin” wrongly lowercases and fuses the name, and “Yi Yin” restores the correct form without otherwise changing the sentence.
Some say, yiyin carry tripod urge Tang wang, Baili Xi feed cow cart under Mu Gong use hegemon, make first match, then lead great way.
Some say, Yi Yin carry tripod urge Tang wang, Baili Xi feed cow cart under Mu Gong use hegemon, make first match, then lead great way.
The same 伊尹 appears in the literal calque as “yiyin”; capitalizing as “Yi Yin” corrects the proper name while leaving the rest of the literal rendering intact.

Xun Qing hated the governance of that turbid age: ruined states and chaotic rulers followed one another, neglecting the great Way while relying on shamans and prayers, trusting in lucky and unlucky omens, and allowing base Confucians to cling to small details without understanding the larger order.

Xun Qing hated the governance of that turbid age: ruined states and chaotic rulers followed one another, neglecting the great Way while relying on shamans and prayers, trusting in lucky and unlucky omens; he despised narrow-minded Confucians, and men like Zhuang Zhou who with slippery facetiousness disordered custom. Thereupon he traced the rise and fall of the conduct of Confucians, Mohists, and Daoists, arranged them in sequence, and wrote tens of thousands of words before he died.
The idiomatic text truncates after 信禨祥 / 鄙儒小拘 and drops 如莊周等又猾稽亂俗 and 於是推儒、墨、道德之行事興壞，序列著數萬言而卒; the proposed restoration matches those Chinese clauses and the complete literal English.
